paper_title: Anisotropic cosmic optical background bound for decaying dark matter in light of the LORRI anomaly
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1 (converted from decay rate Gamma via Gamma = g^2 m^3 / 64pi)
notes: Paper derives a new 95% CL exclusion on the decay rate of eV-scale dark matter decaying to photons from HST measurements of the cosmic optical background (COB) anisotropy, motivated by the New Horizons/LORRI COB excess. Main results: Fig. 2 excludes decay rates Gamma-hat > 1e-24 to 1e-23 s^-1 for m = 5-20 eV; Fig. 3 translates this into the ALP-photon coupling plane (g_agamma vs m_a, axis range ~1e-12 to 5e-10 GeV^-1) assuming ALP is all the cold DM (R=1, q_gamma=2). Exact numerical values are not tabulated; the data_points here are reconstructed from the text-quoted Gamma range (assuming ~1e-23 s^-1 at 5 eV weakening to ~1e-24 s^-1 at 20 eV, with log interpolation) using Gamma = g^2 m^3 / (64 pi). Values are consistent with the Fig. 3 axis range but are approximate (factor ~2 uncertainty). This is a cosmological (extragalactic) bound, so no local DM density assumption applies.
